title: Getting Started
content: Getting Started XL Converter is a powerful image converter for the latest formats. Installation Download Page Only download XL Converter from codepoems.eu. Windows Double-click on the downloaded file. A warning may appear. Click on More Info (link) Run Anyway (button) Windows shows this warning on all software without an expensive digital certificate. More info Next, follow the installer. Linux Unpack the 7z archive Run ./install.sh Image Viewers These image viewers support AVIF and JPEG XL. Windows ImageGlass - easiest to use XnViewMP / IrfanView (with plugins) / PicView / PhotoQt / nomacs - alternatives Linux AVIF Install this package. sudo apt install libavif-gdk-pixbuf Detailed tutorial JPEG XL For security-conscious Linux users, sticking with AVIF may be preferable. Download the latest binaries for your distribution. Unpack then install them sudo dpkg -i *deb Detailed tutorial

title: Adding Files
content: Adding Files Add files (or folders) by dragging and dropping them onto the program. This works on every tab. Alternatively, use the buttons at the bottom. Add Files - add selected files Add Folder - add all files from a folder (and its subfolders)

title: Choosing Output
content: Choosing Output All these options are located in the Output tab. Save To Source Folder Each image will be saved in the same folder as its source. Custom All images will be saved to that particular folder. If a folder doesn't exist, it will be created. Copy and paste a path or click on the button with 3 dots to use a dialog. There are two types of paths: Absolute path (e.g. C:/Images/Converted) Relative path (e.g. Converted) - saves to a folder of that name next source image Keep Folder Structure - preserves the original folder hierarchy when saving images. Conversion Duplicate - what to do when a file with the same name already exists in the output directory. Threads - how much of your CPU to dedicate for conversion. Higher means faster. Setting it to max is not advisable If you're actively using your computer. After Conversion Clear File List - file list in the input tab will be cleared after conversion. Delete Original - the image you added to the list will be deleted after it's converted.

title: Formats
content: Formats Formats - Overview Estimation compression efficiency. Format Lossy Lossless Compatibility Transparency JPEG XL High High Low Yes AVIF High - Medium Yes WEBP Medium Medium Medium-High Yes JPG Low - High No PNG - Low High Yes Formats - Lossy JPEG XL Quality 90 - visually lossless 80 - high quality and reasonable size 60 - space saving sweet-spot Effort - higher is better 7 - normal speed and good quality 9 - slower speed and better quality. May result in bigger (or smaller) files. When combined with Modular, files are always smaller. Intelligent Effort - prioritizes smaller file sizes Lossy Mode - Modular Disabled - best for photos and complex images Enabled - best for images with sharp edges and flat areas, like digital art, screenshots or documents Learn more about modes in JPEG XL AVIF Quality - higher is better quality and bigger size 90 - visually lossless 70 - reasonable quality and file size 50 - medium quality 30 - bad quality Speed - lower is slower, better quality, and smaller file size 6 - normal speed 0 - very slow, best quality and smallest size WEBP Quality 90 - great quality and large file size 80 - good compromise between quality and size 60 - looks fine only far away Chroma Subsampling Controls color compression. Lower number means less color information and smaller file size. Default - usually picks 4:4:4, but tries to match the input 4:4:4 - full color, highest quality and file size 4:2:2 - less color (small visual difference) and significant space saving 4:2:0 - colors may appear washed out 4:0:0 - grayscale Learn more If you are confused, just leave it at default. JPG Encoder JPEGLI from JPEG XL - extremely fast and high quality, and space efficient. ImageMagick - stable, trusted, and tested. Great at preserving noise. Formats - Lossless Lossless encoding is available for JPEG XL, WEBP or PNG. Smallest Lossless Converts to multiple formats, then picks the smallest one. Can save up to 25% of space. The checkboxes control which formats will be used. While JPEG XL features the most efficient lossless compression on average, other formats can outperform it on certain images. Remember the bit depth limits of each format. JPEG XL automatically appends JPG reconstruction data in this mode.

title: Downscaling
content: Downscaling Downscaling is available in the Modify tab. All methods maintain the same aspect ratio. They only scale the image down, not up. Resolution Clamps the resolutions to fit in the selected range. Percent Scales to that percentage. Example: 80% will result in both width and height being 80% of the original values. Shortest and Longest Side Makes a particular side fit to the selected resolution. File Size Scales image to desired file size (approximately). It is about 4 times slower than regular conversion. It uses linear regression to predict image scale. Its accuracy varies, so use other modes whenever possible. You can preserve higher resolution by decreasing the quality (in the Format Tab). Resampling Methods You can enable custom resampling in the Settings Tab (Custom Resampling checkbox). You should not change this unless you know a lot about resampling. By default, Lanczos will be used. Notes Intelligent Effort (in JPEG XL) is compatible with all downscaling types Downscaling is unavailable for animated images and in the "Smallest Lossless" mode

title: Metadata
content: Metadata All metadata options are located in the Modify Tab. Encoder These options are recommended for most users. They are faster and less likely to cause any issues. However, their effectiveness varies. Wipe - wipes metadata. Preserve - preserves metadata. How encoders respect those preferences. Format Encoder - Wipe Encoder - Preserve JPEG XL Yes Yes AVIF Yes Yes WEBP Yes Yes JPG (ImageMagick) Yes Yes JPG (JPEGLI) No No PNG Varies Varies ExifTool ExifTool will handle your metadata more thoroughly, but the conversion will take longer. Safe Wipe - deletes all metadata except the one affecting the final image. Preserve - copies over all metadata. Unsafe Wipe - deletes every last bit of metadata, including color profile. It can potentially alter the final image. Corresponding commands Safe Wipe - exiftool -all= -tagsFromFile @ --icc_profile:all --ColorSpace:all -overwrite_original <dst> Preserve - exiftool -tagsfromfile <src> -overwrite_original <dst> Unsafe Wipe - exiftool -all= -overwrite_original <dst> Notes Preserving metadata is challenging because image formats are rarely 100% compatible with one another. If your metadata holds significant value, consider using ExifTool directly to export it to text files. Exceptions The following behavior may differ from what's expected. Format Mode Note JPG -> JPEG XL (lossless) Encoder - Wipe All metadata is preserved to ensure JPG can be fully reconstructed.

title: JPG Reconstruction
content: JPG Reconstruction Overview This feature allows you to preserve the original JPG while lowering its file size by 15% - 25% You can reconstruct the original JPG file at any moment. Encoding Reconstruction Data Add JPG files Select JPEG XL format in the Output tab Check Lossless Convert Reconstruction data will be added automatically If the input format is a JPG Increasing the Effort will reduce the file size. Reconstructing JPG Add JXL files Select PNG format Check Reconstruct JPG from JPEG XL Convert A JPG will be generated instead of a PNG, If reconstruction data is found

title: Shortcuts
content: Shortcuts General Alt + 1 - 5 - switch to a tab Input Tab Ctrl + A - select all Ctrl + Shift + X - clear list Delete - delete selected entries Up or Down - navigate up or down the list Home - move to the top of the list End - move to the bottom of the list Shift + Home - select all items above Shift + End - select all items below Select Range - click an item, hold shift then click on another.

title: Troubleshooting
content: Troubleshooting Bug Reports You can submit a bug report in 2 ways [public] - Submit a new GitHub Issue [private] - Email me at contact@codepoems.eu VCOMP140.DLL was not found Install Visual C++ Redistributable 2015 - 2022. This is needed for ImageMagick to work. Running out of RAM (JPEG XL) This is only a problem for unreasonably large images. Set Effort to 7 and uncheck Modular. Image viewers may fail to open JPEG XL images of extreme sizes. ~libjxl issue

title: FAQ
content: FAQ Is XL Converter safe? Of course! The source code is publicly available (and auditable). Just make sure you are getting it from the official website - codepoems.eu or the GitHub repo. What technologies are used? JPEG XL, JPG - libjxl AVIF - libavif (AOM AV1) JPG, WEBP, Downscaling - ImageMagick XL Converter was written in Python and PySide6.

title: Settings
content: Settings The default is usually the best. Make sure you really know what you're doing before changing anything. General Dark Theme - the intended look of XL Converter Disable Downscaling on Startup - disables downscaling when you when you launch the application. Disable Delete Original on Startup - unchecks delete original when you when you launch the application. Disable Exception Popups - the pop-up displaying errors encountered during conversion will no longer appear. Input - Disable Sorting - disables sorting in the Input Tab, has no impact on performance. Conversion JPEGLI - Disable Progressive Scan - generated JPGs will be compatible with very old devices, but their file size will increase. WEBP - Method - lowering it will make encoding WEBP faster, but will also lower the quality and increase the file size. Advanced JPEG XL - Enable Effort 10 (slow) - raises Effort limit from 9 to 10. Effort 10 is very slow but can produce smaller files in lossless. Downscaling - Custom Resampling - enables resampling mode selection in the Modify Tab. Custom Encoder Parameters - additional params for the encoders. Make sure all parameters you add are valid; otherwise, the encoder will stop working.

title: JPEG XL vs AVIF
content: JPEG XL vs AVIF Lossy Efficiency Both JPEG XL and AVIF offer great image quality with different strengths. Recommended uses: JPEG XL Photographs Large Images (8k) Scanned Documents AVIF Screenshots Digital Art Synthetic Imagery Visual Comparison Images have been cropped and upscaled. The differences may not be noticeable in everyday use. Photos JPEG XL (VarDCT, Quality 90) - 3.7 MiB AVIF (Quality 90) - 4.6 MiB JPEG XL yields a smaller size and produces fewer artifacts than AVIF in photos with high-quality preset. Experts may prefer it for its high bit-depth and high-resolution support. On the other hand, AVIF produces sharper images in medium to low-quality presets. Digital Art JPEG XL (Modular, Quality 80) - 167 KiB AVIF (Quality 80) - 168 KiB AVIF performs best on images with sharp edges and flat areas. It also maintains accurate colors and prevents discolored spots. Note It's hard to make an accurate comparison, so try comparing yourself. Convert an image to both formats, import them into a canvas in GIMP, then toggle between the layers. Lossless JPEG XL lossless mode offers the best efficiency. WEBP may perform better on certain images, but on average JPEG XL is the best. Conversion Speed Higher is better Format Encoder Speed JPG JPEGLI 10.26x JPG ImageMagick 1.09x JPEG XL libjxl 1x AVIF libavif 0.7x Speed / Effort were set to default. Input format was PNG. Capabilities Feature JPEG XL AVIF Max Resolution 1,073,741,823 x 1,073,741,823 *65536 x 65536 Max Bit Depth 32 bit 12 bit Compatibility Low High Lossy Excellent Excellent Lossless Excellent Bad Encoding Speed Fast Slow Transparency Yes Yes Security Average Good Additional Features JPEG Reconstruction *Only 8193 x 4320 natively, larger sizes are achieved with tiling (which lowers efficiency beyond that point) Technical State While JPEG XL is more future-oriented, it's still in its early stages. Bugs are to be expected. The JPEG XL repo states the following: "Note: This release is for evaluation purposes and may contain bugs [...]" AVIF is more stable in my experience. Additional Information It's important to note that both AVIF and JPEG XL significantly outperform HEIF. Consider not using HEIF as its license makes it hard to support. Samples: Digital Art / Photos XL Converter uses AOM-AV1 for AVIF. Other AV1 encoders do not match its quality.
